content:
In the 47-person case, 12 defendants filed appeals, which were dismissed by the Court of Appeal in February this year; 11 of them subsequently applied to the Court of Appeal again for a certificate of leave to appeal to the Court of Final Appeal. The Court of Appeal will announce its decision next Monday (the 10th), with the ruling expected to take about five minutes.

In February this year, the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeals of the 12 defendants.

In the 47-person case, 45 defendants were convicted of conspiracy to subvert state power. Among them, 12 defendants — including Yang Xueying, Wong Pik-wan, Chow Ka-sing, Yu Wai-ming, Gigi Ho, Lam Cheuk-ting, Ng Ching-hang, Cheng Tat-hung, Ho Kai-ming, Chan Chi-chuen, Leung Kwok-hung, and Wong Tsz-yuet — previously filed appeals, all of which were dismissed in late February this year; the Department of Justice's appeal against Lau Wai-lun's acquittal was also dismissed.

Excluding Wong Tsz-yuet, the 11 defendants applied again to appeal to the Court of Final Appeal, seeking a certificate of leave to appeal from the Court of Appeal; the 11 were sentenced to imprisonment ranging from 78 to 93 months. Among them, Gigi Ho appealed against her conviction, while the other ten appealed against both conviction and sentence. According to the Judiciary's website, the Court of Appeal will announce its decision next Monday (the 10th), with the ruling expected to take about five minutes.

The Court of Appeal dismissed the appeals of the 12 defendants in February this year, ruling that the trial judge's determination that the defendants were members of the conspiracy was 'beyond reproach.' However, regarding whether the Basic Law permits legislators to force the Chief Executive to be held accountable by vetoing the financial budget, the Court of Appeal considered the matter to be of important constitutional significance but declined to make a ruling, stating that the parties' submissions were 'superficial.' On sentencing, the Court of Appeal also held that the seven-year starting point for imprisonment was not manifestly excessive and endorsed the original sentence.
